name: rapibase-backend-tools
description: Postgres, auth, pgvector, S3 storage, server functions, and app deployment in one backend.

interface.longDescription: Build and run apps with Postgres, authentication, pgvector, S3-compatible storage, server functions, and deployment in one Rapibase project. Four skills guide schema design, access rules, functions, releases, logs, and troubleshooting. Connect your Rapibase account with OAuth to use the MCP tools. The connection can reach only the projects and permissions you authorize.
defaultPrompt: Show my Rapibase projects and their status.
Help me design a database for my app.
Find errors in my Rapibase project logs.

positive.description: The reviewer account has one running Rapibase review project authorized through OAuth. Verify account-scoped project discovery and status without exposing credentials.
positive.prompt: Show the Rapibase projects this connection can access and tell me which are running.
positive.expected_behavior: Call list_projects once. Report only the projects, access modes, and statuses returned by the tool. Do not invent projects or show API keys.

positive.description: The authorized review project contains a sample table named review_items with columns id and name and at least two sample rows. Verify schema discovery and a read-only data query.
positive.prompt: In my Rapibase review project, describe the review_items table and show its first two rows.
positive.expected_behavior: Use list_projects to obtain the authorized project slug. Call describe_table with that project and table=review_items, then query_rows with the same project, table=review_items, page=1, and page_size=2. Report column types and only the rows actually returned.

positive.description: The same review project grants write access and its review_items table accepts a name value. Verify a user-requested insert and readback of sample data.
positive.prompt: Add a sample item named OpenAI review item to the review_items table in my Rapibase review project, then show me the inserted row.
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve the authorized review project with list_projects. Use describe_table if needed, then call insert_row with project set to that slug, table=review_items, and data containing name='OpenAI review item'. Show the row returned by insert_row, including its generated id if present. Never claim insertion if the tool reports an error.

positive.description: The reviewer account can inspect storage in its authorized review project. This case works whether or not the project has buckets.
positive.prompt: List the storage buckets in my Rapibase review project and summarize their access settings and usage.
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve the review project using list_projects and call list_buckets with its project slug. Report only returned bucket settings and usage. If there are no buckets, state that the list is empty; do not invent buckets or files.

positive.description: The reviewer account can inspect the review project's server functions, frontend releases, and recent app logs. Verify deployment and operational inspection without publishing a new release.
positive.prompt: Check my Rapibase review project: what server functions and frontend releases are there, and do the recent app logs show errors?
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve the authorized review project with list_projects. Call list_functions, list_deploys, and get_logs for the same project (container='app'). Summarize only the returned functions, releases, and log errors. If a list is empty or logs show no errors, say so; do not claim a deployment occurred.

negative.description: A request about another backend provider. Explain that the Rapibase connection cannot inspect Supabase projects; do not call any Rapibase MCP tool or invent access.
negative.prompt: Show me the tables in my Supabase project. I have not connected Supabase here.

negative.description: A deployment request for a different hosting provider. Explain that the Rapibase connection cannot deploy to Vercel; do not call any Rapibase MCP tool or claim a deployment.
negative.prompt: Deploy my website to Vercel and give me its production URL.

negative.description: A domain-management request outside Rapibase. Explain that changing Cloudflare DNS requires access to Cloudflare; do not call any Rapibase MCP tool or claim a DNS change.
negative.prompt: Change the DNS records for my domain in Cloudflare to point to a new server.

publication.release_notes: Initial release of Rapibase backend tools: guidance for Postgres, authentication, storage, server functions, deployment, and troubleshooting, with account-scoped MCP access through OAuth.
